mechanism_log: The system has 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inactive inputs (X7-X12). Y3 is driven by X1 and X3 with a synergistic interaction (X1*X3). Y4 is driven by X2(+), X4(+), X1(weak+), X6(-). Y1 is driven by all of X1-X6 positively, but X6's effect on Y1 depends strongly on X5 (sign switches from negative to positive as X5 increases — a critical X5*X6 interaction). Y2 is driven by X1(-), X3(-), X4(-), X2(+), X6(+). The objectives conflict: X2 and X6 increase both Y1 and Y2, while X3 and X4 improve Y1 while decreasing Y2. Y3 threshold requires sufficient X1 and X3 (synergistic, so both must be moderate-to-high).

X2 is nearly linear across its range: Y1 +0.33, Y2 +0.08, Y4 +0.17, Y3 zero.
X4-X6 interaction is mild (std≈0.015) despite dramatic gradient shifts seen when ALL inputs varied simultaneously.
Y2 regression has R²=0.91, well explained by linear model: X3(-0.20), X6(+0.15), X4(-0.10), X2(+0.10), X1(-0.08).
surprises: X1-X3 interaction on Y3 was SYNERGISTIC (amplifying), not antagonistic (saturating) as predicted. Each input amplifies the other's effect. This means Y3≥0.4 constraint requires BOTH to be at moderate levels, not just one at high.
X4-X6 interaction was much weaker than expected (std=0.015). The dramatic gradient changes at extreme corners were driven by OTHER inputs changing simultaneously, not X4-X6 coupling specifically.

X5 appears as a pure moderator: it has no direct effect on any output but strongly controls X6's sign on Y1. The regression coefficient of 0.31 for X5→Y1 is misleading — the effect is entirely through interaction with X6.
X1 has a small but real positive effect on Y4 (range 0.06), which was predicted as flat from center gradient of 0.027.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Test the X5*X6 interaction formally with interaction_test to quantify the sign-switching behavior on Y1 and Y2. Then shift to optimization: use the causal model to design Pareto-optimal configurations. Key trade-off axis is X2/X6 (increase Y1+Y4 but also Y2) vs keeping them low (better Y2 but worse Y1/Y4). X3 and X4 should be set high (win-win for most objectives). X1 and X3 must be sufficiently high for Y3≥0.4 constraint.
